solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discover and pass back a note

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a mountain pass is read the other way round

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
te is the seventh note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Someone finds something and hands a note back to a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests handing over, but it is a mountain col; 'note' is the sol-fa syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight synonym: to discover something is to find where it is.

clue.text: Star embraced by girl in entertainment centre

indicators.note: embraced by means the star's name is held inside the word for girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity hugged by a girl at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but it is the astronomical star Vega.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous worldwide for casinos and shows.

clue.text: Those who enjoy getting high?

parts.note: drug users seem meant, but it is people who scale heights

explanation.surface: A sly reference to drug takers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting high' suggests drugs; the question mark flags the literal sense of going up mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers and rock scalers literally reach high places for pleasure.

clue.text: Refuse to fold over the sheet

definitions.meaning: to fold back a bedsheet's top edge

explanation.surface: Someone declines to fold the bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: rejecting an offer, and folding back bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to decline an offer and to fold back bedding.

clue.text: Joint vote cast in Irish parliament

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the parliament's name

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A combined vote is held in the Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective describing the vote, but it is the definition, a carpentry joint. 'cast' and 'in' are the anagram and container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a type of woodworking joint with interlocking wedge-shaped pieces.

clue.text: A singular method of dealing with a traffic problem

parts.note: a singular thing is just one
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: An unusual solution to congestion on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' seems to mean odd, but it means just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricting a street to one direction of travel is a common fix for congestion.

clue.text: I've found it in a Greek dictionary

definitions.text: I've found it in a Greek dictionary

parts.words: I've found it in a Greek dictionary
parts.note: the exclamation that Archimedes made, which is a Greek word meaning I have found

explanation.surface: Someone triumphantly locating a word in a Greek lexicon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek word translates as 'I have found it', attributed to Archimedes in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation literally translates the phrase given, so a Greek lexicon would gloss it so.

clue.text: I am included in an American's hostility

indicators.note: included in places the contraction inside the other letters

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for American
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being part of an American's animosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am' contracts, as in speech, and 'included in' puts that inside the article and the country's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: animus is ill will, animosity or enmity.

clue.text: The long version lacks nothing in measurement

definitions.text: The long version lacks nothing in measurement

parts.words: The long version lacks nothing in measurement
parts.note: the noun form of long, used as a dimension, a word for how far something extends

explanation.surface: An extended edition is complete and well measured.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun made from 'long' is a measurement; the 'long version' is the adjective's noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a measured extent from end to end, made from the adjective long.

clue.text: Sportsmen on mountains, right in their heaven

indicators.note: in says the letter for right goes inside the word for heaven

parts.note: the skies is a poetic word for heaven

explanation.surface: Skiers on the slopes are happiest, in their own private heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: People who ski are sportsmen whose sport is played on snowy mountains.

clue.text: Former Russian, American or English architecture

definitions.meaning: someone from Georgia, once part of the Soviet Union
someone from the US state of Georgia
the style of building from the reigns of the four Georges, 1714 to 1830

explanation.surface: A list of building styles: former Russian, American or English architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the nation in the Caucasus, the US state, and the British period style.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a person or style named after Georgia or the Hanoverian kings called George.

clue.text: Incorporate dome by reconstruction

indicators.note: reconstruction means the letters are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: An architect plans to add a dome by rebuilding the structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to incorporate something is to include or give it bodily form.

clue.text: By no means on one's uppers

definitions.meaning: read literally: having no means, no money at all
a British idiom for being very poor, worn down to the uppers of one's shoes

explanation.surface: An emphatic denial that someone is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By no means' reads as 'not at all', but it is literal: without means. 'On one's uppers' is British slang for destitute, soles worn through.
explanation.definitionFit: A person declared insolvent has no money, the plight both phrases describe.

clue.text: Be born healthy, getting an advantage

parts.note: ne (French née) marks the birth name, so it stands for born
fit means in good health

explanation.surface: Being born healthy gives a child a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a benefit is a gain or an advantage.

clue.text: Operator of a lock and harbour, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for harbour is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a quay is a harbour wharf

explanation.surface: A lock keeper on a canal working near the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a canal lock beside a harbour, but it is a door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is the device that turns or operates a lock.

clue.text: New wars or old weapons

indicators.note: new indicates the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Modern wars or older weapons: a comparison of warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges WARS OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: bows and their projectiles were the missile weapons of earlier eras.

clue.text: The appeal of love on board ship

indicators.note: on board places one piece between the letters for a ship, as a passenger on deck

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The romance of a cruise: love aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' means a call for help, not attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Morse distress signal is an urgent appeal for help.

clue.text: Drink up for Indian government

indicators.note: up signals the word is written bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, especially a pint

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to the authorities in India.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jar' is British slang for a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names British rule over the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Used for jotting down music?

parts.note: a pad for jotting down notes, read playfully as musical notes

explanation.surface: Something a composer uses to scribble down a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the item is for jotting memos, not musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for memos and short written reminders.

clue.text: Finished dance when the playing stops

parts.note: dead means finished, over
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dance ends when the band stops playing.
explanation.walkthrough: In sport, the ball is out of play between incidents.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby, the state when play is temporarily halted.

clue.text: Withdraw Jack's pamphlet

parts.note: a jack and an AB (able seaman) are both sailors, so jack's gives AB plus S
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Pulling a sailor's pamphlet from circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, like an AB.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to take out or remove.

clue.text: Naval vessels which should be quarantined?

definitions.text: Naval vessels which should be quarantined?

parts.words: Naval vessels which should be quarantined?
parts.note: warships for aircraft, punningly also people who spread disease

explanation.surface: Warships held offshore because of an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: The word also means people who carry infection, hence the quarantine.
explanation.definitionFit: Large warships launch aircraft; the same word names those who transmit illness.

clue.text: Ear job operation for rodent

indicators.note: operation suggests the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon carries out an ear job on a small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' sounds surgical, but it rearranges EAR JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a jerboa is a small jumping desert rodent of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Party when out of range of Russia

indicators.note: out of means the word for when is taken away

parts.note: the Caucasus is a mountain range in southern Russia
as means when, as in as the sun rose

explanation.surface: A party group meeting when beyond the reach of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a political meeting, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting of a political faction to choose candidates or policy.

clue.text: Clever people are quick on it

definitions.text: Clever people are quick on it

parts.words: Clever people are quick on it
parts.note: the idiom about bright people understanding things fast

explanation.surface: A remark that smart people act fast.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'quick on the uptake'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means comprehension, as in the idiom for fast understanding.

clue.text: Support in reverse

explanation.surface: Help given while travelling backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a noun for reinforcement, and a verb phrase for driving backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a standby resource, and driving a car rearwards.

clue.text: Tease about Eve's origins?

definitions.meaning: to make fun of someone in a good-natured way
in Genesis, Eve was made from one of Adam's bones

explanation.surface: Teasing someone about the story of how Eve came to be.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible God makes Eve from a bone taken from Adam's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a verb meaning to mock gently, and the bone of Eve's creation.

clue.text: Fame secure now? No question about it

indicators.note: about it says the answer lies within the words, around the question

explanation.surface: Is lasting fame secure? Definitely, no question.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides inside 'secuRE NOW? No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: renown is widespread fame or celebrity.

clue.text: Every letter is written in it

definitions.text: Every letter is written in it

parts.words: Every letter is written in it
parts.note: the full set of letters, from A to Z, is set out in this

explanation.surface: A person's correspondence is all written in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence, but it means the characters of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The complete set of letters used to write a language contains every one of them.

clue.text: He's in charge but often has a leader

definitions.text: He's in charge but often has a leader

parts.words: He's in charge but often has a leader
parts.note: the head of a newspaper writes or oversees the leading article

explanation.surface: A boss who nonetheless answers to someone above him.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' is a newspaper's main opinion article, not a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's chief runs the paper and usually has a leading article each day.

clue.text: Prize joke comes first — it's laughable

indicators.note: comes first says the word for joke goes in front of the word for prize

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a joke
a pot is a prize, as in a pot of winnings or a trophy cup

explanation.surface: A comedian's prize-winning joke is a real laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes first' reverses the clue's order of the two pieces; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, an eccentric, absurd idea is ridiculous enough to be mocked.

clue.text: Run a horse in Maine

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Racing a horse somewhere in the state of Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like racing the horse, but it means to be in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to run a business is to be in control of it.

clue.text: Extensive cleaning operation

definitions.meaning: the action of brushing a floor clean

explanation.surface: A big, thorough clean-up job.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: an adjective for wide-ranging and the noun for brushing with a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: wide-ranging changes, and the act of using a broom.

clue.text: Instruments still playable without their heads

definitions.text: Instruments still playable without their heads

parts.words: Instruments still playable without their heads
parts.note: take the first letter off these wind instruments and other stringed instruments remain

explanation.surface: Musical instruments that still work even when broken at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the F and the word left names lutes, also instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind instruments whose names, beheaded, give another family of instruments.
